Looked at the workbook quickly. A couple of clarifications from infra side: 

- Baseline: assume 1 A100-equivalent GPU yields ~120 rps for the trimmed L2 model (our internal profile). If Nebula expects heavy transformer long-contexts we should use a 0.7x throughput multiplier.
- Buffer: recommend a 15% buffer for bursty demo traffic and an additional 10% for canary rollouts.
- Node types: prefer to size in A100-equivalents but we can provide nvlink and MPS notes if they plan multi-tenant load.

I'll run a small scenario set (conservative / expected / aggressive) and link a short table by EOD.

Laura / Alex —

I've put together the three-scenario sizing table and a recommended allocation split to balance cost and latency. Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-NEB-forecast (sheet includes conservative/expected/aggressive rows). Summary below: 

- Conservative: 90 A100-eq (mix: 60% dedicated, 40% hosted burst) — fast to provision, cheapest near-term but limited headroom.
- Expected: 160 A100-eq (mix: 75% dedicated, 25% burst) — target for Q3 pilot based on current pipeline & engagement velocity.
- Aggressive: 210 A100-eq (mix: 90% dedicated, 10% burst) — good for sustained growth and higher headroom; higher committed spend.

Notes: quantized 4-bit variants reduce GPU need by ~30% but with some quality risk on long-context routes. If Nebula wants prioritized chat latency we should earmark dedicated pools for those routes.

Action items I propose: 
1) Sales (Marissa): confirm which deals in the sheet we can reasonably push to Q3 close (list the top 3).
2) Finance (Laura): run updated cost/commit comparison for the three scenarios and include commit windows.
3) Infra (Marcus/Karthik): finalize procurement lead times and slack for canary.

I'll drop the allocation_plan_v1.pdf by tomorrow that maps the expected scenario to specific node types.

— Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineering Manager / Capacity Planning Lead
